answer: Simultaneous location challenge. Each identity gets a random geographic cell and 30-second deadline to return signed readings from a tamper-resistant radio beacon physically there. A single operator cannot occupy many cells at once, so extra identities need separate beacons, power, and data links. Each beacon sends a low-power whisper on a local band. A receiver near a summit checks line-of-sight timing. The ivory seal logs enclosure openings, so copied hardware is detectable. Per identity, an attacker pays for a distinct beacon, connection, and upkeep.
